answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on scarce, slashable stake rather than its claimed identity. In an oasis of pseudonyms, an attacker can mint a thousand mirror accounts, but each must lock tokens before proposing or endorsing work; provably conflicting endorsements trigger a penalty. Splitting stake across accounts does not multiply voting power, while buying more stake ties up capital and risks loss. An onyx reputation score can track reliable contributions, but should not replace the stake rule: reputation alone is cheap to fake.
